help.intro: Three questions, three prepositions, three cases — and one table that answers all of them. For a place you can be inside (Kino, Schule, Supermarkt): Woher? aus dem / aus der — Wo? im / in der — Wohin? ins / in die / in den. For people, activities and the doctor (Anna, Arzt, Sport, Arbeit): von — bei — zu: vom Arzt, beim Arzt, zum Arzt. Cities and most countries: aus Berlin — in Berlin — nach Berlin; countries with an article keep it: aus der Schweiz — in der Schweiz — in die Schweiz. And home is its own set: von zu Hause — zu Hause — nach Hause. Whether you say gehe or fahre depends only on how you get there (on foot or by vehicle); the preposition does not change: Ich gehe ins Kino, ich fahre nach Berlin. The Wo? column is dative, the Wohin? column with in is accusative — that is the two-way preposition rule that comes later in the course, seen here through its most common examples.
help.tips[0].title: Places you enter: aus – in – in
help.tips[0].text: Woher? aus dem Kino / aus der Schule. Wo? im Kino / in der Schule. Wohin? ins Kino / in die Schule / in den Park. The accusative (ins, in die, in den) means you are going in.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I'm going to the cinema. I'm at the cinema. I'm coming from the cinema.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The children go to school. At one they come out of school.
help.tips[0].trap: 'in the cinema' is one phrase in English for both being there and going there. German switches im (dative, Wo?) and ins (accusative, Wohin?).
help.tips[0].check.q: Wir sind heute Abend ____ Theater. (We're at the theatre tonight; das Theater)
help.tips[0].check.why: Being somewhere answers Wo? and takes the dative: in + dem = im. ins would mean going in.
help.tips[1].title: People and activities: von – bei – zu
help.tips[1].text: vom Arzt / von Anna / von der Arbeit — beim Arzt / bei Anna / bei der Arbeit — zum Arzt / zu Anna / zur Arbeit. All dative, no accusative here.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I'm going to the doctor. I'm at the doctor's. I'm coming from the doctor's.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: This evening I'm at Anna's, afterwards I'm going to Tom's.
help.tips[1].check.q: Ich habe Zahnschmerzen. Morgen gehe ich ____ Zahnarzt.
help.tips[1].check.why: Going to a person such as the dentist is zu + dem = zum; beim means you are already there.
help.tips[2].title: Cities and countries: aus – in – nach
help.tips[2].text: aus Berlin – in Berlin – nach Berlin. With an article: aus der Schweiz – in der Schweiz – in die Schweiz (not nach!). aus den USA – in den USA – in die USA.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: She's going to Vienna, then to Switzerland.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: My boss is from Berlin. Next week we are going to Berlin.
help.tips[2].check.why: die Türkei keeps its article, so going there is in die, not nach.
help.tips[3].text: Ich bin zu Hause (I'm at home). Ich gehe nach Hause (I'm going home). Two different phrases; English has one.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Are you at home? – No, I'm on my way home right now.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: On Sunday we're staying at home.
help.tips[3].check.q: Es ist schon spät. Ich gehe jetzt ____.
help.tips[3].check.why: Going home is nach Hause; zu Hause means you are already at home.
help.remember[0]: aus–in–in for buildings, von–bei–zu for people, aus–in–nach for cities.
help.remember[1]: zu Hause = at home, nach Hause = (going) home.
help.context.en: Where are you? – I'm still at work, but I'm going to the supermarket in a minute. – And after that? – After that I'm going home. Are you coming too? – I've just come from school and I'm going to Anna's. I'll be home at eight. – Good, then we'll go to the cinema at nine!
help.mistakes[0].why: Going somewhere is Wohin?: accusative ins.
help.mistakes[1].why: Countries with an article take in, not nach.
help.mistakes[2].why: Going home is nach Hause; zu Hause is being there.
help.vocab[6].en: at the doctor's / to the doctor's
help.hook: Say where someone is, where they're going and where they've come from — im Kino, ins Kino, aus dem Kino.
sentences[0].english: Tonight we're going to the cinema.
sentences[0].why: Going INTO the building: in + accusative, in das = ins — ins Kino.
sentences[1].english: Where are you? – I'm still at the cinema.
sentences[1].why: Being there (wo?) takes the dative: in dem = im Kino.
sentences[2].english: I've just come from the café.
sentences[2].why: Out of the building (woher?): aus + dative — aus dem Café.
sentences[3].english: Are you coming to the café?
sentences[3].why: Heading in (wohin?): in + accusative — ins Café.
sentences[4].english: The children are at school until one.
sentences[4].why: Position, not movement: in + dative — in der Schule.
sentences[5].english: At one the children come home from school.
sentences[5].why: Coming from it: aus der Schule — aus + dative for leaving a building.
sentences[6].english: I'm popping to the supermarket, we've got no bread.
sentences[6].why: Movement in: in den Supermarkt — wohin? turns der into den.
sentences[7].english: Dad's at the supermarket doing the shopping.
sentences[7].why: He is inside (wo?): im Supermarkt — dative.
sentences[8].english: I've got a temperature, I'm going to the doctor.
sentences[8].why: To a person: zu + dative — zum Arzt.
sentences[9].english: She's just come from the doctor's and has a prescription.
sentences[9].why: Back from a person: von + dative — vom Arzt, the return trip of zum Arzt.
sentences[10].why: AT a person's place: bei — bei Anna.
sentences[11].english: After school I'm going to Anna's.
sentences[11].why: TO a person: zu — zu Anna; bei is for being there, zu for going.
sentences[12].english: Every Tuesday he comes home tired from sport.
sentences[12].why: Back from an activity: von — vom Sport.
sentences[13].why: Being at work: bei der Arbeit — bei + dative for the place you are.
sentences[14].english: At seven I go to work.
sentences[14].why: Going there: zu, and zu der contracts to zur — zur Arbeit.
sentences[15].english: Next week we're going to Berlin.
sentences[16].why: Origin from a city: aus — aus Berlin.
sentences[17].english: In winter we're going to Switzerland.
sentences[17].why: die Schweiz has an article, so wohin? is in + accusative: in die Schweiz.
sentences[18].why: Living there is wo?: in + dative — die becomes der: in der Schweiz.
sentences[19].english: It's late, I'm going home now.
sentences[19].why: Going home is the fixed phrase nach Hause.
sentences[20].english: On Sunday we're staying at home.
sentences[20].why: Being home is zu Hause — nach for the way, zu for being there.
sentences[21].english: The bus goes to the station.
sentences[21].why: Heading to the station: zu + dative — zum Bahnhof.
sentences[22].english: I'll wait for you at the station.
sentences[22].why: Waiting AT the station (wo?): an + dative — am Bahnhof.
sentences[23].english: She's sitting in the café drinking tea.
sentences[23].why: Sitting inside (wo?): in + dative — im Café.
